title: MBA Admissions Checklist
subtitle: Step-by-Step Roadmap to Secure Admits at Top Global Business Schools

sections.title: Why an MBA Admissions Checklist Is Essential

blocks.text: Applying for an MBA at top schools (Harvard, Wharton, INSEAD, LBS, ISB) is like running a marathon—you need structure, stamina, and a plan. Many strong candidates fail not because they lack potential but because they mismanage **deadlines, storytelling, or fit.**
An admissions checklist ensures you approach this strategically, not reactively. Each step—resume, essays, recommendations—must align to tell a **coherent narrative.**

blocks.label: Reflection
blocks.text: Write why you want an MBA in 1–2 sentences. Career pivot? Faster leadership growth? Global exposure?

sections.title: Clarify Your MBA Goals (Short & Long Term)

blocks.text: Admissions committees don’t want “general ambition.” They want **clarity.**

items: **Short-Term Goal (2–3 years post-MBA):** Consulting at Bain, Finance at JP Morgan, Product at Amazon.
**Long-Term Goal (10+ years):** Partner, CFO, Entrepreneur, Policy Leader.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Write one short-term and one long-term goal in 2 lines each.

rows: Short term (2–3 years after the MBA)

sections.title: Select the Right Schools – Dream, Target, Safety

blocks.text: Use the **DTS framework**:

items: Dream: Harvard, Stanford, INSEAD.
Target: Duke Fuqua, LBS, ISB.
Safety: Tier-2 programs that still match goals.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: List 2–3 schools in each DTS bucket.
Schools differ in culture, strengths, and networks. Example:

items: INSEAD = international diversity + consulting placements.
Wharton = finance powerhouse.
LBS = London exposure + global mobility.
ISB = India focus + global faculty.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Pick 1 school. Write 2 strengths and how they align with your goals.

sections.title: Build a Competitive Resume for Admissions

blocks.text: Your admissions resume should highlight:

items: Leadership: Did you lead teams/projects?
Impact: Did you save costs, increase revenue, influence strategy?
Extracurriculars: Volunteer, sports, NGOs.
Don’t recycle job CVs—they’re too task-heavy.
Focus on leadership potential and quantifiable achievements.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Rewrite 1 resume bullet with numbers + leadership focus.
Essays = your **voice.** They must:

items: Answer why MBA, why now, why this school.
Showcase personal values & resilience.
Tell unique stories—not clichés.
Instead of “I want to lead,” show: “During a crisis project, I aligned 5 teams across geographies to deliver under budget.”

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Draft 3 bullet points from your life you could expand into essay stories.
Your recommender should be:

items: Someone who **knows you well.**
Can speak about leadership & growth.
Aligned with your essays (no contradictions).

blocks.text: Provide them a **recommendation packet**: your resume, essays, and 3 key stories they can highlight.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Write 2 names of potential recommenders.

items: **GMAT/GRE:** Aim at or above the median score in each target school’s latest class profile.
**IELTS/TOEFL:** Needed if undergrad wasn’t in English.
Prep tip: Practice 1 hr/day for 6–9 months.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Write your target score + exam date.
MBA apps = project management.

items: Round 1: September–October (often the best scholarship chances).
Round 2: January–February (a larger applicant pool).
Round 3: riskier; use it only for backup schools.

blocks.label: Worksheet
blocks.text: Build a calendar with GMAT prep, essay drafts, and submission deadlines.
MBA interviews test **fit + communication.**

items: Common Qs: “Why MBA?” “Why this school?” “Leadership story?”
Practice with **mock interviews.**

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Record a 2-min answer to “Why MBA now?” and review for clarity.
Funding is often overlooked. Options:

items: Merit scholarships (ISB, Oxford).
Need-based aid (Harvard, Stanford).
Loans: Prodigy Finance, MPower, Indian banks.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: List 2 funding sources you’d explore.

items: **An Indian business school admit:** Aarav, a chartered accountant at a Big Four firm, wrote essays about leading through client crises. Result: an admit with a 30% scholarship.
**A European business school admit:** Maria, a consultant, highlighted her international mobility and growth mindset. Result: an admit with a scholarship.

blocks.label: Lesson
blocks.text: Storytelling + clarity + funding prep = success.

items: Mistakes: Generic essays, weak recommenders, late submissions.
Fix: Start early, build strong stories, align every element.
